nominees.name: Chandrashekhar Joshi
nominees.affiliation: University of California, Los Angeles, USA

motivation: In 1979 Tajima (with the late J. M. Dawson) proposed that an intense laser pulse in a plasma drives a wake whose fields exceed those of conventional accelerators by three orders of magnitude. Joshi pioneered the experimental demonstration of plasma-wave acceleration, first with beat-wave and later with electron- and laser-driven wakes, reaching energy doubling of 42 GeV electrons in under a metre. Malka led decisive experiments producing quasi-monoenergetic, then tunable and stable, electron beams from laser-plasma accelerators, and turned them into compact sources of femtosecond X-rays. Together they opened a new frontier: accelerating gradients of 100 GV/m, GeV beams from centimetre-scale plasmas, and compact light sources now used in imaging and ultrafast science. Laser-plasma accelerators also provide the multi-GeV electron beams that have allowed the first laboratory tests of radiation reaction and strong-field QED, linking fundamental theory to measurable signals.
